sections.overview: This Venezuelan species occurs in the lower Caura and middle and upper Orinoco drainages.
sections.identification: A dark stripe extends from the eye to the corner of the preopercle; the original description separates it from G. grammepareius by several anatomical and colour traits.
sections.habitat: A Swedish cichlid registry describes sandy stream beds and shallow margins with vegetation or woody debris.
sections.diet: It sifts sand while foraging, as described in the regional habitat account.
sections.behavior: Species-specific social behaviour is not detailed in the sources consulted.
sections.reproduction: The accounts consulted do not provide a confirmed species-specific breeding description.
sections.ecology: G. grammepareius shares the cheek stripe but is limited to the upper Caura and lower Caroní; G. dicrozoster instead has a preopercular mark and lacks the complete stripe. G. gottwaldi shares its complete stripe but has a larger rectangular flank blotch and larger pale tail spots.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports global Least Concern, assessed on 28 October 2020.
